newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.N. recovers funds in embezzlement scandal.
newsitem.headline: U.N. recovers funds in embezzlement scandal.

text.p: The United Nations has recovered more than two-thirds of an estimated 731,000 Swiss francs ($500,000) allegedly embezzled by a former employee, a top official said on Tuesday.

Karl-Theodor Paschke, under-secretary-general for internal oversight services, also said that a Geneva magistrate had completed his investigation into the year-old case and had made his recommendations to the public prosecutor.
The case involves an ex-employee of the U.N. trade and development agency UNCTAD, identified only as an American of Cuban origin. The man is currently detained at a guarded medical facility.
If the Geneva prosecutor lays formal criminal charges against him, it would be the first such case against a U.N. worker in the world body's European headquarters.
The U.N. stripped the employee of his diplomatic immunity to allow the probe, an UNCTAD spokesman said. "We are hopeful he will be charged," he added.
UNCTAD disclosed last May that it had filed a criminal complaint against the man, saying he was suspected of fraud and embezzlement over some 20 years. It suspended him without pay.
"Today the U.N. has recovered more than two-thirds of the total damages which according to our investigation were caused by this former staff member," Paschke told a news briefing.
"As far as recovery of damages, recently we and the former staff member have signed an agreement under which he has committed himself to repairing the damage he caused to the U.N."
Andrew Whitley, UNCTAD's head of external relations, said that former U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros Ghali had dismissed the employee last December on grounds of "gross misconduct".
"The U.N. believes the amount embezzled was 731,000 Swiss francs," Whitley told Reuters. "We stopped investigations going more than 10 years back because bank records have been destroyed."
He said funds had been recovered from several countries.
The alleged fraud was discovered by another UNCTAD staffer temporarily replacing the man, who was on sick leave at the time.

Paschke, noting the case was still with the Swiss judicial system, said corrective measures have already been taken in the wake of the affair. "I am confident this type of case cannot repeat itself," he said.
